title: Protocol for electrical modulation of ERK signaling dynamics in cell lines
protocol: Pre-coat the chambers to accelerate cell adhesion.
Load 5 μL of coating solution (Collagen or FNC Coating Mix®) into each chamber using a 20 μl pipette from one side.
Aspirate on the other side to remove air bubbles.
Add 200 μl culture medium to the far end of each reservoir.
Allow cells to adhere for around 2–3 h and fill the reservoirs with more medium after cells are attached.
Use a Pasteur pipette attached to a vacuum line to aspirate any remaining air bubble in the chamber.
Cover the plate and incubate for 5 (for coating with FNC) to 30 (for coating with 20 μg/mL collagen I) min in a sterile hood.
Remove the coating solution by aspiration.
Gently rinse the chamber once with sterile PBS.
Prepare target cell suspension.
Rinse MCF10A cells expressing ERKTR-mCherry twice with 3 ml PBS in a T25 flask.
Trypsinize MCF10A cells expressing ERKTR-mCherry with 2 mL 0.05% trypsin and 0.53 mM EDTA for 15–20 min following ATCC’s protocol.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding 4 mL culture medium or 2 mL 0.1% soybean trypsin inhibitor.
Collect the single cell suspension after gentle pipetting.
Adjust cell concentration to approximately 5 × 10^5/mL after counting.
Seed cells in the stimulation chamber.
Remix the cell suspension gently every 2 min by shaking or using a large gauge pipette tip and pipetting gently.
Load 10 μL cell suspension through one side of the chamber.
Aspirate using a 2 μL pipette from the other side if needed to remove air bubbles.
Gently add 200 μL cell culture medium to the far end of each reservoir without connecting to the cell suspension in the chamber.
Add PBS to all spaces in the plate between the PDMS device and the dish.
Cover the plate.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for about 2 h.
Check cells using an inverted microscope.
Gently add additional 0.5 mL growth medium to each medium reservoir when cells are fully attached.
Incubate cells 12–18 h at 37°C with 5% CO2 to allow cells to fully attach.
Aspirate culture medium from both reservoirs of each chamber.
Rinse the chamber 3 times with PBS to remove unattached cells and growth factors in the old medium.
Fill the chambers with serum-free, growth factor-free medium to starve cells.
Incubate cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 3 h.
Aspirate the medium from the imaging chamber.
Wash the reservoirs twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of low fluorescence imaging medium to each reservoir.
Transfer the dish containing starved cells to be studied to the temperature-controlled chamber of the imaging system.
Mount the dish securely on the microscope stage.
Set the temperature to 37°C and allow it to stabilize for 20–30 minutes before mounting the dish.
Switch on the CO2 control module when needed.
Cover the dish using a sterilized lid with holes on it.
Align the holes of the lid to the reservoirs.
Mount the Ag/AgCl electrodes, placing one electrode in each reservoir.
Dip the tip of the electrodes in the medium.
Connect the electrodes with the AC power supply via electric cables.
Fill two beakers with Steinberg’s solution and immerse electrodes in the solution.
Connect the beakers of Steinberg’s solution to the medium reservoirs of the stimulation chambers with pre-made agar glass bridges through the holes on the lid.
Switch on and adjust the voltage across the AC chamber using a standard voltage meter.
Mount platinum wires through an extra pair of holes between the electrodes and seal the holes with 3140 silicone rubber if necessary.
Start the image acquisition software and set up parameters required for time-lapse recording.
Select the objective according to experimental demand.
Bring the imaging window of the stimulation chamber into focus.
Navigate to an XY position to select 2 or more regions of interest (ROI) in each chamber for multi-field time-lapse recording.
Try to avoid regions where cells are overcrowded.
Ensure that the ROI positions are located sufficiently apart to minimize photobleaching and phototoxicity.
Select appropriate filters and dichromatic mirrors to acquire differential interference contrast (DIC) images and images of Cyan-fluorescent and red-fluorescent protein fusions.
Determine optimal exposure time for each channel.
Use DIC 100 msec, RFP 300 msec, CFP 500 msec as exposure times in settings.
Adjust the focus manually at each ROI as necessary.
Set auto-focus for DIC channel with a step accuracy of 0.5–1 μm in a range of 3 μm.
Run autofocus routinely for each time point to correct for focal drift.
Set the autofocus strategy to “update z-positions after each acquisition” if available.
Set up a time series to acquire images at the desired time points in sequence.
For investigating the effects of AC stimulation on ERK activation, select a 30–60 s time interval over a 2 h period.
For long-term monitoring of ERK dynamics controlled by the AC with optimized parameters, select a 5 min time interval over a 5–24 h period.
Give it a dry run by clicking the acquisition button without any AC stimulation.
Stop image recording after finishing the second frame of all ROIs.
Check images to confirm correct focus and exposure settings have not shifted during multi-position acquisition.
Start the time-lapse experiment by clicking the acquisition button again.
Image cells for 5–30 min before any stimulation to acquire a baseline signal.
Switch on the AC with desired voltage, frequency, and waveform to stimulate cells in each chamber.
Use a time relay to automatically control the on and off duration of AC stimulation.
Monitor the voltage during stimulation and adjust it if needed.
Check that all stage positions are still in focus at later points.
Pause imaging acquisition if refocusing is required due to stage drift, then resume imaging within defined intervals.
Stop image acquisition at a defined time point.
Shut down the computer and microscope.
Remove the PDMS chamber and fix the cells immediately after stimulation for immunostaining if needed.
Launch ImageJ program to generate time-lapse movies.
Import the imaging file using “File>Import>Image sequence”.
Adjust the numbers of “Starting image” and “Increment” in the “Image sequence” to obtain separate image stacks for each illumination channel (DIC, RFP, CFP) of each ROI position.
Optional: Adjust the brightness and/or contrast by clicking “Image>Adjust>Brightness/Contrast” or pressing “Ctrl”+“Shift”+“C” for a better view of the images.
Crop the images to exclude non-cell areas and minimize file size to accelerate subsequent quantification processes.
Use the “Rectangular Selection” tool to select a smaller ROI in the DIC image stack and duplicate the stack of ROI with “Ctrl”+“Shift”+“D”.
Crop the same ROI for RFP and CFP stacks using "Edit>Selection>Restore Selection" and pressing “Ctrl”+“Shift”+“D”.
Save cropped image stacks as single “.tiff” files.
Data analysis to extract single-cell kinetics.
Connect the AC EF stimulation chamber with the AC power supply through a pair of agar salt bridges.
Image cells seeded in the AC stimulation chambers using a fully automated fluorescence microscope with an incubation chamber to maintain optimal culture conditions.
Apply AC EFs through a pair of Ag electrodes with the desired stimulation scheme controlled by a digital time relay.
Monitor the output voltage using a voltmeter connected in parallel with the stimulation chamber.
Record time-lapse images using Metamorph software.
Import .tiff stacks into MATLAB for image segmentation, tracking, and intensity quantitation.
Identify the nuclear region based on the nuclear localization of EKAR3 containing a nuclear import sequence.
Define the cytosolic region as the neighboring 7-pixel area outside the identified nuclear region.
Calculate cell ERKTR level as Fc/Fn, where Fc is the RFP fluorescence intensity of the cytosol and Fn is that of the nucleus.
